records.source: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אֵלִיָּ֨הוּ הַתִּשְׁבִּ֜י מִתֹּשָׁבֵ֣י גִלְעָד֮ אֶל־אַחְאָב֒ חַי־יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָמַ֣דְתִּי לְפָנָ֔יו אִם־יִהְיֶ֛ה הַשָּׁנִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה טַ֣ל וּמָטָ֑ר כִּ֖י אִם־לְפִ֥י דְבָרִֽי׃ס
records.gloss: And said Elijah the Tishbite, from [the] settlers of Gilead, to Ahab, [As] lives Yahweh, God of Israel, whom I stand before his face, if there will be [in] the years these dew and rain, except at [the] mouth of my word.
pieces: Elijah the Tishbite, one of the settlers in Gilead, said to Ahab, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, lives, whom I serve, there will be neither dew nor rain in the years ahead unless I give the word."

L.1: And Elijah the Tishbite, from the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there will be no dew or rain these years, except at my word."

R.1: Elijah the Tishbite, who lived among the settlers in Gilead, went to King Ahab. He said, "I serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel. As surely as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lives, there will be no dew and no rain during the next few years until I say so."

decisions.choice: from the settlers of Gilead
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text, as its vowels read it, calls Elijah one of the settlers of Gilead: people who lived there as residents without belonging to an old family of the land. The same letters can be read as "from Tishbe of Gilead", and the ancient Greek translation reads them so. That reading fits the title "the Tishbite" just before, but no town called Tishbe in Gilead is known for certain. The Hebrew text as read is kept here.

decisions.choice: Elijah the Tishbite: a prophet from Gilead, east of the Jordan, sent to King Ahab
decisions.reason: Elijah appears here with no account of his family or his call. "Tishbite" names the place or group he came from, whose location is now unknown. His name means "my God is Yahweh", which suits his whole work against the worship of Baal. Ahab was the king of Israel who had built a temple for Baal in Samaria (16:29-33).

decisions.choice: as Yahweh lives, before whom I stand: a solemn oath, and a claim to serve Yahweh
decisions.reason: Swearing by the life of Yahweh is the strongest oath (1 Samuel 14:39; 20:3). To "stand before" someone is to serve him as an attendant stands ready before a king (10:8; 12:8). Elijah speaks as Yahweh's servant and messenger, not by his own authority.

decisions.choice: if there will be dew or rain: the form of an oath meaning there will be none
decisions.reason: In an oath, "if this happens" leaves a curse unspoken, so it means "this will not happen". "Except at the mouth of my word" means "unless I say so": the drought will end only when Elijah, speaking for Yahweh, announces it (18:1, 41).

decisions.choice: no dew or rain: a challenge to Baal, who was worshiped as the giver of rain
decisions.reason: In the dry summer the land depends on dew, and in winter on rain. Baal, whom Ahab now served (16:31-32), was believed to send both. Yahweh's word stops them, which shows who truly controls the rain (18:1, 38-45).

decisions.choice: whom I serve (Balanced); I serve (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "before whom I stand" means, as meaning decision m3 explains. Literal keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: King Ahab; went to
decisions.reason: Readable names Ahab's title and says that Elijah went to him, since the story begins suddenly. Readable also puts the oath after Elijah's statement that he serves the LORD, to keep its sentences short.

records.heading: Elijah announces a drought

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֥יו לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to him, saying,
pieces: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Elijah:

L.2: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to him, saying,

R.2: Then a message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Elijah:

decisions.choice: the word of Yahweh came to him: Yahweh spoke to him as a prophet
decisions.reason: This is the usual way of saying that Yahweh gave a prophet a message (1 Samuel 15:10; 2 Samuel 7:4). Here it is an order telling Elijah where to go.

decisions.choice: Elijah (for "him"); a message (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Elijah for clarity. Readable says "message" for "word", since the word is a whole message, as in 1 Samuel 15:10.

records.source: לֵ֣ךְ מִזֶּ֔ה וּפָנִ֥יתָ לְּךָ֖ קֵ֑דְמָה וְנִסְתַּרְתָּ֙ בְּנַ֣חַל כְּרִ֔ית אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: Go from here, and turn yourself eastward, and hide yourself at [the] wadi of Cherith, which [is] on [the] face of the Jordan.
pieces: "Leave this place and turn east. Hide by the Wadi Cherith, east of the Jordan.

L.3: "Go from here and turn eastward, and hide yourself by the wadi Cherith, which [is] facing the Jordan.

R.3: "Leave here and go east. Hide by Cherith Creek, east of the Jordan River.

decisions.choice: the wadi Cherith: a narrow valley with a seasonal stream
decisions.reason: A wadi is a valley cut by water that flows in the rainy season and can dry up in the dry months, as this one does (verse 7). Its exact location is unknown.

decisions.choice: on the face of the Jordan: east of the Jordan
alternatives: near the Jordan, on either side
decisions.reason: The phrase means "facing" the Jordan. Since Elijah is told to turn east, it most likely places the wadi on the east side of the river, near his home region of Gilead (verse 1).

decisions.choice: hide yourself: keep out of Ahab's reach
decisions.reason: After his message to Ahab, Elijah is in danger. Ahab later searches every nation for him (18:10), and the queen kills Yahweh's prophets (18:4).

decisions.choice: the Wadi Cherith (Balanced); Cherith Creek (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps "Wadi" as part of the name, as with the Wadi Besor (1 Samuel 30:9). Readable names the stream, which is what Elijah drinks from.

records.source: וְהָיָ֖ה מֵהַנַּ֣חַל תִּשְׁתֶּ֑ה וְאֶת־הָעֹרְבִ֣ים צִוִּ֔יתִי לְכַלְכֶּלְךָ֖ שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And it will be, from the wadi you will drink, and the ravens I have commanded to feed you there.
pieces: You will drink from the stream, and I have ordered the ravens to bring you food there."

L.4: And it will be [that] you will drink from the wadi, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there."

R.4: You can drink water from the stream. And I have commanded the ravens to feed you there."

decisions.choice: the ravens
decisions.reason: The Hebrew vowels read "the ravens", and verse 6 shows birds bringing food morning and evening. The same letters with other vowels could be read as "the Arabs", or as people from a place called Arabah, and some have preferred that reading because it seems more natural. But the story presents a wonder, and the text as read is kept.

decisions.choice: ravens: unclean birds that eat carrion
decisions.reason: Ravens were among the birds Israel was not to eat (Leviticus 11:15). Yahweh uses these unlikely creatures to feed his servant, as he feeds even the ravens themselves (Job 38:41; Psalm 147:9).

decisions.choice: I have commanded: the order is already given
decisions.reason: The verb looks at the command as already settled. Yahweh has provided before Elijah arrives, as he will also do with the widow (verse 9). "Feed" is a word for keeping someone supplied with food.

decisions.choice: bring you food
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "feed" means here: the ravens do not feed Elijah by hand but bring him food (verse 6).

records.source: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ וַיַּ֖עַשׂ כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ וַיֵּ֨שֶׁב֙ בְּנַ֣חַל כְּרִ֔ית אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃
records.gloss: And he went and did according to [the] word of Yahweh; and he went and dwelt at [the] wadi of Cherith which [is] on [the] face of the Jordan.
pieces: So Elijah did as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told him. He went and stayed by the Wadi Cherith, east of the Jordan.

L.5: So he went and did according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; he went and lived by the wadi Cherith, which [is] facing the Jordan.

R.5: So Elijah obeyed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. He went and lived by Cherith Creek, east of the Jordan River.

decisions.choice: he went and did according to the word of Yahweh: exact obedience
decisions.reason: The narrator repeats the words of the command (verse 3) to show that Elijah did just what he was told. The same pattern marks the widow's obedience to Elijah's word (verse 15).

decisions.choice: Elijah (for "he")
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Elijah. Readable says "obeyed" for "did according to the word".

records.source: וְהָעֹרְבִ֗ים מְבִיאִ֨ים ל֜וֹ לֶ֤חֶם וּבָשָׂר֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְלֶ֥חֶם וּבָשָׂ֖ר בָּעָ֑רֶב וּמִן־הַנַּ֖חַל יִשְׁתֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And the ravens [were] bringing to him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and from the wadi he drank.
pieces: The ravens brought him bread and meat every morning and every evening, and he drank from the stream.

L.6: And the ravens were bringing him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening, and he drank from the wadi.

R.6: Every morning and every evening the ravens brought Elijah bread and meat. And he drank water from the stream.

decisions.choice: were bringing: this happened day after day
decisions.reason: The verb describes something that went on regularly, not a single delivery.

decisions.choice: bread and meat, morning and evening: an echo of the manna and the quails
decisions.reason: In the wilderness Yahweh gave Israel meat in the evening and bread in the morning (Exodus 16:8, 12). Here Elijah, alone in a dry place, receives both twice a day. "Bread" can also mean food in general.

decisions.choice: every morning and every evening
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable combine the two repeated phrases, which says the same thing more naturally. Readable names Elijah for "him".

records.source: וַיְהִ֛י מִקֵּ֥ץ יָמִ֖ים וַיִּיבַ֣שׁ הַנָּ֑חַל כִּ֛י לֹֽא־הָיָ֥ה גֶ֖שֶׁם בָּאָֽרֶץ׃ס
records.gloss: And it was at [the] end of days, and dried up the wadi, because there had not been rain in the land.
pieces: After a while the stream dried up, because there had been no rain in the land.

L.7: And it happened at the end of days that the wadi dried up, because there was no rain in the land.

R.7: But after some time the stream dried up, because no rain had fallen anywhere in the land.

decisions.choice: at the end of days: after some time
decisions.reason: The phrase gives no exact length. "Days" can sometimes mean a year (1 Samuel 1:21; 27:7), so it may mean "after a year", but the text does not say.

decisions.choice: the wadi dried up: Elijah himself feels the drought he announced
decisions.reason: The prophet who spoke the word is not spared its effects. Yahweh provides for him, but step by step, and now sends him elsewhere.

decisions.choice: anywhere in the land
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the drought covered the whole land.

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֥יו לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to him, saying,
pieces: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Elijah:

L.8: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to him, saying,

R.8: Then a message from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Elijah:

decisions.choice: the word of Yahweh came to him
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: Elijah (for "him"); a message (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.heading: The widow of Zarephath

records.source: ק֣וּם לֵ֤ךְ צָרְפַ֨תָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְצִיד֔וֹן וְיָשַׁבְתָּ֖ שָׁ֑ם הִנֵּ֨ה צִוִּ֥יתִי שָׁ֛ם אִשָּׁ֥ה אַלְמָנָ֖ה לְכַלְכְּלֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Arise, go to Zarephath, which [belongs] to Sidon, and dwell there; look, I have commanded there a woman, a widow, to feed you.
pieces: "Get up and go to Zarephath, a town of Sidon, and stay there. I have commanded a widow there to provide for you."

L.9: "Arise, go to Zarephath, which [belongs] to Sidon, and live there. Look, I have commanded a widow woman there to feed you."

R.9: "Get up and go to the town of Zarephath in the land of Sidon. Stay there. I have told a widow there to give you food."

decisions.choice: Zarephath of Sidon: a town on the coast, in Jezebel's homeland
decisions.reason: Zarephath lay on the Mediterranean coast between Tyre and Sidon, outside Israel. Sidon was the land of Jezebel's father, the king who served Baal (16:31). Yahweh sends his prophet into the heart of Baal's own country.

decisions.choice: I have commanded a widow to feed you: Yahweh has arranged it
decisions.reason: The same words were used of the ravens (verse 4). The widow does not seem to know of any command when Elijah meets her (verse 12), so the sense is that Yahweh has already decided she will provide for him. A widow had no husband to support her and was among the poorest people in the land (Deuteronomy 10:18).

decisions.choice: a town of Sidon (Balanced); the town of Zarephath in the land of Sidon (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Which belongs to Sidon" means that Zarephath was under Sidon, the main city of the region. Readable adds "town" and "land" for readers who do not know the names.

records.source: וַיָּ֣קָם׀וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ צָרְפַ֗תָה וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל־פֶּ֣תַח הָעִ֔יר וְהִנֵּֽה־שָׁ֛ם אִשָּׁ֥ה אַלְמָנָ֖ה מְקֹשֶׁ֣שֶׁת עֵצִ֑ים וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר קְחִי־נָ֨א לִ֧י מְעַט־מַ֛יִם בַּכְּלִ֖י וְאֶשְׁתֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And he arose and went to Zarephath, and he came to [the] entrance of the city, and look, there a woman, a widow, [was] gathering sticks; and he called to her and said, Get, please, for me a little water in the vessel, and I may drink.
pieces: So he got up and went to Zarephath. When he came to the town gate, there was a widow gathering sticks. He called to her, "Please bring me a little water in a cup so I can drink."

L.10: So he arose and went to Zarephath. And he came to the entrance of the city, and look, there a widow woman [was] gathering sticks. And he called to her and said, "Please get me a little water in a vessel, so that I may drink."

R.10: So Elijah went to Zarephath. When he came to the town gate, he saw a widow there picking up sticks. He called out to her, "Please bring me a little water in a cup to drink."

decisions.choice: the entrance of the city: the town gate
decisions.reason: The gate was the busiest place in a town, where people met, traded and settled disputes. Elijah meets the widow as soon as he arrives.

decisions.choice: look, there a widow: the very woman Yahweh spoke of
decisions.reason: "Look" brings the reader into what Elijah saw: a widow, just as Yahweh had said (verse 9).

decisions.choice: gathering sticks; a little water: signs of poverty and drought
decisions.reason: She gathers sticks for a small fire, and water has become scarce. Asking a stranger for water was a normal request (Genesis 24:17), but in a drought it was a real gift. "Please" makes the request polite.

decisions.choice: cup
decisions.reason: The word means any container. Balanced and Readable say "cup", the kind of vessel someone would drink from.

records.source: וַתֵּ֖לֶךְ לָקַ֑חַת וַיִּקְרָ֤א אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר לִֽקְחִי־נָ֥א לִ֛י פַּת־לֶ֖חֶם בְּיָדֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And she went to get [it], and he called to her and said, Get, please, for me a piece of bread in your hand.
pieces: As she was going to get it, he called after her, "Please bring a piece of bread with you too."

L.11: And she went to get [it], and he called to her and said, "Please get me a piece of bread in your hand."

R.11: As she was going, he called to her again, "Please bring me a piece of bread too."

decisions.choice: in your hand: bring it with you
decisions.reason: Elijah asks her to bring the bread along with the water. He asks for only a piece, but in a famine even that is more than she can spare (verse 12).

decisions.choice: too
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "too" to show that this request is added to the first. Readable leaves "in your hand" unsaid, since "bring" already says it.

records.source: וַתֹּ֗אמֶר חַי־יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ אִם־יֶשׁ־לִ֣י מָע֔וֹג כִּ֣י אִם־מְלֹ֤א כַף־קֶ֨מַח֙ בַּכַּ֔ד וּמְעַט־שֶׁ֖מֶן בַּצַּפָּ֑חַת וְהִנְנִ֨י מְקֹשֶׁ֜שֶׁת שְׁנַ֣יִם עֵצִ֗ים וּבָ֨אתִי֙ וַעֲשִׂיתִ֨יהוּ֙ לִ֣י וְלִבְנִ֔י וַאֲכַלְנֻ֖הוּ וָמָֽתְנוּ׃
records.gloss: And she said, [As] lives Yahweh your God, if there is to me a cake, except only [the] fullness of [a] palm of flour in the jar and a little oil in the jug; and look, I [am] gathering two sticks, and I will go in and make it for myself and for my son, and we will eat it and we will die.
pieces: She said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God lives, I have nothing baked, only a handful of flour in the jar and a little oil in the jug. I am gathering a couple of sticks so I can go home and prepare it for my son and me. We will eat it, and then we will die."

L.12: And she said, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God lives, I have no cake, only a handful of flour in the jar and a little oil in the jug. And look, I [am] gathering two sticks, and I will go in and make it for myself and for my son, and we will eat it and die."

R.12: She answered, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God lives, I do not have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour in a jar and a little olive oil in a jug. I am picking up a few sticks to take home and make a last meal for my son and me. After we eat it, we will die."

decisions.choice: as Yahweh your God lives: she swears by the God of Elijah
decisions.reason: She uses the same oath as Elijah (verse 1), but says "your God". She knows Elijah is an Israelite who worships Yahweh, and does not claim Yahweh as her own God. "If there is to me" is the form of an oath meaning "there is not" (see verse 1).

decisions.choice: cake: something baked
decisions.reason: The word is rare (Psalm 35:16) and means baked bread or a cake. She has flour, but nothing ready to eat.

decisions.choice: the jar and the jug: a storage jar for flour and a small jug for oil
decisions.reason: The first is a clay jar of the kind used to carry water or store grain (Genesis 24:14). The second is a small flask for oil, which was olive oil used in cooking.

decisions.choice: two sticks: a few sticks
decisions.reason: "Two" means only a small number, enough for one small fire.

decisions.choice: a last meal
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear what she means: this is the last of her food, and after it she expects to starve. Readable also says "olive oil".

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלֶ֤יהָ אֵלִיָּ֨הוּ֙ אַל־תִּ֣ירְאִ֔י בֹּ֖אִי עֲשִׂ֣י כִדְבָרֵ֑ךְ אַ֣ךְ עֲשִׂי־לִ֣י מִ֠שָּׁם עֻגָ֨ה קְטַנָּ֤ה בָרִאשֹׁנָה֙ וְהוֹצֵ֣אתְלִ֔י וְלָ֣ךְ וְלִבְנֵ֔ךְ תַּעֲשִׂ֖י בָּאַחֲרֹנָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And said to her Elijah, Do not fear; go, do according to your word; only make for me from it a cake small at first, and bring [it] out to me, and for yourself and for your son make at last.
pieces: Elijah said to her, "Do not be afraid. Go and do what you said. But first bake me a small loaf from what you have and bring it out to me. After that, make something for yourself and your son.

L.13: And Elijah said to her, "Do not fear. Go, do according to your word. Only make me a small cake from it first, and bring [it] out to me, and afterward make [some] for yourself and for your son.

R.13: Elijah said to her, "Do not be afraid. Go home and do what you said. But first make a small loaf of bread for me from what you have, and bring it to me. After that, make some for yourself and your son.

decisions.choice: do not fear: reassurance before a promise
decisions.reason: "Do not fear" often comes just before Yahweh's promise of help (Genesis 15:1; 21:17). Elijah's reason follows in verse 14.

decisions.choice: a small cake: a round flat loaf
decisions.reason: The word names a flat round bread, baked on hot stones or coals (Genesis 18:6; 19:3).

decisions.choice: first ... afterward: Elijah asks her to feed him before herself
decisions.reason: The words "first" and "at last" frame the request. Elijah asks her to put the word of Yahweh to the test by giving away her last food first. "Bring it out" suggests that she bakes inside and brings it out to him.

decisions.choice: small loaf
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "loaf", since an English "cake" is usually sweet.

records.source: כִּ֣י כֹה֩ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כַּ֤ד הַקֶּ֨מַח֙ לֹ֣א תִכְלָ֔ה וְצַפַּ֥חַת הַשֶּׁ֖מֶן לֹ֣א תֶחְסָ֑ר עַ֠ד י֧וֹם תֵּת־יְהוָ֛ה גֶּ֖שֶׁם עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָאֲדָמָֽה׃
records.gloss: For thus says Yahweh, God of Israel, [The] jar of the flour not will be finished, and [the] jug of the oil not will be lacking, until [the] day [that] gives Yahweh rain on [the] face of the ground.
pieces: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: 'The jar of flour will not be emptied, and the jug of oil will not give out, until the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sends rain on the land.'"

L.14: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: 'The jar of flour will not be used up, and the jug of oil will not run short, until the day [that] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives rain on the face of the ground.'"

R.14: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: 'Your jar of flour will not become empty, and your jug of oil will not run out, until the day {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} sends rain on the land again.'"

decisions.choice: thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel: a prophet's message formula
decisions.reason: A messenger began by naming who sent him. Elijah gives the widow a promise in Yahweh's own words. He calls Yahweh "the God of Israel" even in Sidon: Israel's God, not Baal, keeps a foreign widow alive.

decisions.choice: until the day Yahweh gives rain
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has a different form of the verb "give" from the one read aloud in the tradition, but both mean the same.

decisions.choice: until Yahweh gives rain: the drought is in Yahweh's hands
decisions.reason: The promise looks ahead to the end of the drought (18:1, 45). The same God who stopped the rain will send it, and until then he will provide.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (Literal); the LORD says this (Balanced); This is what the LORD says (Readable)
decisions.reason: The message formula is worded the same way throughout Samuel and Kings. Yahweh's words inside Elijah's speech take single quotes. Readable adds "again" to make clear the rain will return, and says "your" jar and jug, since the promise is about the widow's own supplies.

records.source: וַתֵּ֥לֶךְ וַתַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה כִּדְבַ֣ר אֵלִיָּ֑הוּ וַתֹּ֧אכַל הִֽיא־וָה֛וּא וּבֵיתָ֖הּ יָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: And she went and did according to [the] word of Elijah; and ate she and he and her household [many] days.
pieces: She went and did as Elijah had said, and she and he and her household had food to eat for many days.

L.15: And she went and did according to the word of Elijah, and she and he and her household ate [for many] days.

R.15: So she went and did what Elijah told her. And there was food every day for her and her family and for Elijah.

decisions.choice: she and he
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew text has "he and she"; the form read aloud in the tradition has "she and he". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: days: for a long time
decisions.reason: The bare word "days" means for many days, perhaps for a whole year (as in verse 7). The food lasted as long as it was needed.

decisions.choice: she went and did according to the word of Elijah: her obedience matches his
decisions.reason: The widow obeys Elijah's word just as Elijah obeyed Yahweh's (verse 5). "Her household" is her son and perhaps others living with her.

decisions.choice: had food to eat for many days (Balanced); there was food every day (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out what the bare word "days" means.

records.source: כַּ֤ד הַקֶּ֨מַח֙ לֹ֣א כָלָ֔תָה וְצַפַּ֥חַת הַשֶּׁ֖מֶן לֹ֣א חָסֵ֑ר כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר בְּיַ֥ד אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃פ
records.gloss: [The] jar of the flour not was finished, and [the] jug of the oil not was lacking, according to [the] word of Yahweh which he spoke by [the] hand of Elijah.
pieces: The jar of flour was not emptied, and the jug of oil did not give out, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said through Elijah.

L.16: The jar of flour was not used up, and the jug of oil did not run short, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke by the hand of Elijah.

R.16: The jar of flour never became empty, and the jug of oil never ran out. It happened just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had promised through Elijah.

decisions.choice: the promise is fulfilled in its own words
decisions.reason: The narrator repeats the words of verse 14 to show that it happened exactly as Yahweh said.

decisions.choice: by the hand of Elijah: through Elijah
decisions.reason: Yahweh spoke and Elijah delivered the word. "By the hand of" means "through" someone, as a messenger.

decisions.choice: promised
decisions.reason: Readable says "promised" because what Yahweh said was a promise (verse 14).

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה חָלָ֕ה בֶּן־הָאִשָּׁ֖ה בַּעֲלַ֣ת הַבָּ֑יִת וַיְהִ֤י חָלְיוֹ֙ חָזָ֣ק מְאֹ֔ד עַ֛ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־נֽוֹתְרָה־בּ֖וֹ נְשָׁמָֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was after the things these, became sick [the] son of the woman, the mistress of the house, and was his sickness strong very, until that not was left in him breath.
pieces: Some time after this, the son of the woman who owned the house fell ill. His illness grew so severe that at last there was no breath left in him.

L.17: And it happened after these things [that] the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, became sick, and his sickness was very severe, until no breath was left in him.

R.17: Some time later the son of the woman who owned the house got sick. He got worse and worse, until finally he stopped breathing.

decisions.choice: the mistress of the house: the woman who owned the house
decisions.reason: She is head of her own household and has a house with an upper room (verse 19), though she had almost no food. The title also prepares for Elijah's place in her home.

decisions.choice: no breath was left in him: he died
decisions.reason: The word for breath is the breath of life (Genesis 2:7). Some have taken the words to mean that he came near death, but the mother speaks of his death (verse 18), Elijah says Yahweh has caused it (verse 20), and the boy's life must come back (verse 22).

decisions.choice: He got worse and worse
decisions.reason: Readable says in plain words that the illness grew very severe.

records.heading: Elijah raises the widow's son

records.source: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ מַה־לִּ֥י וָלָ֖ךְ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים בָּ֧אתָ אֵלַ֛י לְהַזְכִּ֥יר אֶת־עֲוֺנִ֖י וּלְהָמִ֥ית אֶת־בְּנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And she said to Elijah, What [is] to me and to you, man of God? You have come to me to bring to remembrance my iniquity and to put to death my son!
pieces: She said to Elijah, "What do you have against me, man of God? You came to me to bring my sin to light and to kill my son!"

L.18: And she said to Elijah, "What [is there] between me and you, man of God? You have come to me to bring my iniquity to remembrance and to put my son to death!"

R.18: She said to Elijah, "Man of God, why have you done this to me? You came here to remind God of my sin and to make my son die!"

decisions.choice: what is there between me and you: what quarrel do you have with me?
decisions.reason: The phrase asks why someone is acting against the speaker (Judges 11:12; 2 Samuel 16:10). She blames Elijah for her son's death.

decisions.choice: man of God: a prophet
decisions.reason: "Man of God" is a title for a prophet who speaks and acts for God (1 Samuel 2:27; 1 Kings 13:1). She knows Elijah is holy, and she fears that holiness.

decisions.choice: to bring my iniquity to remembrance: to draw God's attention to her sin
alternatives: to make me remember my sin
decisions.reason: She thinks that the presence of a holy man has made God notice some sin of hers, and that her son's death is the punishment. The text does not say what sin she means. The words could also mean to make her remember her sin; either way she sees the death as judgment.

decisions.choice: you have come: an accusation, not only a question
decisions.reason: The words can be read as a bitter statement or as a question; both carry her charge that Elijah's coming caused the death.

decisions.choice: remind God of my sin
decisions.reason: Readable takes the more likely sense of meaning decision m3 and names God, and asks "why have you done this to me" for the opening idiom.

records.source: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֵלֶ֖יהָ תְּנִֽי־לִ֣י אֶת־בְּנֵ֑ךְ וַיִּקָּחֵ֣הוּ מֵחֵיקָ֗הּ וַֽיַּעֲלֵ֨הוּ֙ אֶל־הָעֲלִיָּ֗ה אֲשֶׁר־הוּא֙ יֹשֵׁ֣ב שָׁ֔ם וַיַּשְׁכִּבֵ֖הוּ עַל־מִטָּתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he said to her, Give to me your son; and he took him from her bosom, and he took him up to the upper room where he [was] dwelling there, and he laid him on his bed.
pieces: "Give me your son," he said to her. He took the boy from her arms, carried him up to the upstairs room where he was staying, and put him down on his own bed.

L.19: And he said to her, "Give me your son." And he took him from her bosom and carried him up to the upper room where he was living, and laid him on his [own] bed.

R.19: Elijah said to her, "Give me your son." He took the boy from her arms and carried him up to the room upstairs where he was staying. He laid him on his own bed.

decisions.choice: the upper room: a room built on the flat roof
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs, and a room could be built on top, reached by an outside stair. It gave a guest a place of his own (2 Kings 4:10).

decisions.choice: her bosom: her arms, held against her chest
decisions.reason: She was holding the dead child close to her.

decisions.choice: his bed: Elijah's own bed
decisions.reason: "His" refers to Elijah, who lays the boy on his own bed in his own room, away from the mother.

decisions.choice: arms
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "arms", the natural English for where she held him.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔י הֲ֠גַם עַל־הָאַלְמָנָ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֨י מִתְגּוֹרֵ֥ר עִמָּ֛הּ הֲרֵע֖וֹתָ לְהָמִ֥ית אֶת־בְּנָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And he called to Yahweh and said, Yahweh my God, also upon the widow whom I [am] staying with her, have you done evil, by putting to death her son?
pieces: Then he cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} my God, have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought disaster even on this widow who has given me a place to stay, by causing her son to die?"

L.20: And he called to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} my God, have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} also brought evil on the widow with whom I am staying, by putting her son to death?"

R.20: Then he cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} my God, have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought trouble even on this widow who lets me stay with her? Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made her son die?"

decisions.choice: also on the widow: even on her, on top of the drought on the whole land
decisions.reason: "Also" places her loss beside the suffering of the drought. She had taken in Yahweh's prophet, and now she too is struck.

decisions.choice: I am staying with her: living as a guest in her house
decisions.reason: The verb is used of living as an outsider among others (Genesis 12:10). Elijah depends on her hospitality.

decisions.choice: have you brought evil: a bold lament
decisions.reason: "Evil" here is harm or disaster, not wrongdoing. Elijah does not hide his distress from Yahweh but asks him directly, as Moses did (Numbers 11:11). He assumes that Yahweh is in control of life and death.

decisions.choice: disaster (Balanced); trouble (Readable); given me a place to stay
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid "evil", which in English suggests wickedness. Readable splits the question in two.

records.source: וַיִּתְמֹדֵ֤ד עַל־הַיֶּ֨לֶד֙ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ פְּעָמִ֔ים וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶל־יְהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔י תָּ֥שָׁב נָ֛א נֶֽפֶשׁ־הַיֶּ֥לֶד הַזֶּ֖ה עַל־קִרְבּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he stretched himself upon the child three times, and he called to Yahweh and said, Yahweh my God, let return, please, [the] life of the child this to his inward parts.
pieces: Then he stretched himself out over the boy three times and cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} my God, please let this boy's life come back into him!"

L.21: And he stretched himself out on the child three times, and he called to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} my God, please let the life of this child return into him."

R.21: Then Elijah lay down on the boy three times, stretching his body over him. He cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} my God, please let this boy live again! Let his life come back into him!"

decisions.choice: stretched himself on the child: lay over the boy's body
decisions.reason: The verb means "measured himself", that is, stretched out full length over the child. Elisha does something similar for the son of the woman of Shunem (2 Kings 4:34-35). Doing it three times shows how earnestly he pleaded.

decisions.choice: life: the living self
decisions.reason: The word often rendered "soul" here means the life of a person, which leaves at death and returns when life is restored (Genesis 35:18). It is not a separate part of the person.

decisions.choice: into his inward parts: back into him
decisions.reason: "Inward parts" means the inside of the body. Elijah asks that life return to the boy's body.

decisions.choice: boy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable call the child "boy", since he is a son (verse 17). Readable adds "let this boy live again" to say plainly what the prayer asks, and keeps the image of life coming back.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה בְּק֣וֹל אֵלִיָּ֑הוּ וַתָּ֧שָׁב נֶֽפֶשׁ־הַיֶּ֛לֶד עַל־קִרְבּ֖וֹ וַיֶּֽחִי׃
records.gloss: And listened Yahweh to [the] voice of Elijah, and returned [the] life of the child to his inward parts, and he lived.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} listened to Elijah's cry, and the boy's life came back into him, and he lived.

L.22: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} listened to the voice of Elijah, and the life of the child returned into him, and he lived.

R.22: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered Elijah's prayer. The boy's life came back into him, and he was alive again.

decisions.choice: listened to the voice of: heard and granted
decisions.reason: To "listen to the voice" of someone who prays means to grant what he asks (Numbers 21:3).

decisions.choice: he lived: the first account in Scripture of the dead raised to life
decisions.reason: The words of the answer repeat the words of the prayer (verse 21). The God of Israel gives life in the land of Baal, and the boy's living answers the oath "as Yahweh lives" (verses 1, 12).

decisions.choice: cry (Balanced); answered Elijah's prayer (Readable)
decisions.reason: Elijah's "voice" here is his prayer to Yahweh.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אֵלִיָּ֜הוּ אֶת־הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַיֹּרִדֵ֤הוּ מִן־הָעֲלִיָּה֙ הַבַּ֔יְתָה וַֽיִּתְּנֵ֖הוּ לְאִמּ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ רְאִ֖י חַ֥י בְּנֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And took Elijah the child and brought him down from the upper room into the house, and gave him to his mother; and said Elijah, See, alive [is] your son.
pieces: Elijah took the boy, brought him down from the upstairs room into the house, and gave him to his mother. "Look," Elijah said, "your son is alive!"

L.23: And Elijah took the child and brought him down from the upper room into the house, and gave him to his mother. And Elijah said, "See, your son [is] alive."

R.23: Elijah picked up the boy and carried him downstairs into the house. He gave him back to his mother and said, "Look, your son is alive!"

decisions.choice: alive: the key word of the chapter
decisions.reason: The word for "alive" is the same as in the oaths "as Yahweh lives" (verses 1, 12). Yahweh, who lives, has given life back to the boy.

decisions.choice: from the upper room into the house: down to the main living area
decisions.reason: Elijah brings the boy down from the roof room (verse 19) to the rooms below, where his mother was.

decisions.choice: carried him downstairs; gave him back
decisions.reason: Readable says "downstairs" for "from the upper room" and "back" because the boy had been taken from her.

records.source: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר הָֽאִשָּׁה֙ אֶל־אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ עַתָּה֙ זֶ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ אֱלֹהִ֖ים אָ֑תָּה וּדְבַר־יְהוָ֥ה בְּפִ֖יךָ אֱמֶֽת׃פ
records.gloss: And said the woman to Elijah, Now this I know, that [a] man of God [are] you, and [the] word of Yahweh in your mouth [is] truth.
pieces: Then the woman said to Elijah, "Now I know you are a man of God, and that what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says through you is true."

L.24: And the woman said to Elijah, "Now this I know, that you [are] a man of God, and the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in your mouth [is] truth."

R.24: Then the woman said to Elijah, "Now I know that you really are a man of God. What you say comes from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and it is true."

decisions.choice: now this I know: now at last she is sure
decisions.reason: The words stress the moment of knowing. She had called Elijah "man of God" in anger (verse 18); now she says it in faith.

decisions.choice: truth: reliable, to be trusted
decisions.reason: The word means what is firm and can be relied on. Yahweh's word through Elijah has proved true: the flour and oil lasted (verse 16) and her son lives.

decisions.choice: the word of Yahweh in your mouth: Yahweh speaks through Elijah
decisions.reason: The chapter began with Elijah's word stopping the rain (verse 1). It ends with a foreign woman confessing that Yahweh's word through him is true, before the contest with Baal's prophets in chapter 18.

decisions.choice: really
decisions.reason: Readable adds "really" to bring out the force of "now this I know" after her earlier doubt.
